status.en: 199 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 19% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Plateau State.
status.nb: 199 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 19 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Plateau State.

summary.en: Bandits killed four soldiers and 18 civilians in Zamfara and shot an immigration officer, whose body was set ablaze, in Niger. Gunmen ambushed traders and security operatives in Zamfara, killing dozens of civilians and soldiers. ISWAP fighters attacked a military base in Adamawa and a town in Borno, but were repelled after air strikes that killed more than 40 militants, including 25 neutralised. Atiku Abubakar urged security agencies to rescue a family abducted in Kaduna, while the abductors demanded a 300 million-naira ransom. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Banditter drepte fire soldater og 18 sivile i Zamfara og skjøt en immigrasjonsoffiser, hvis kropp ble satt i brann, i Niger. Skytevåpen overfalt handelsmenn og sikkerhetsoperatører i Zamfara, og drepte dusinvis av sivile og soldater. ISWAP-krigere angrep en militærbase i Adamawa og en by i Borno, men ble avverget etter luftangrep som drepte mer enn 40 militante, inkludert 25 nøytraliserte. Atiku Abubakar oppfordret sikkerhetsbyråene til å redde en familie som ble bortført i Kaduna, mens bortførerene krevde en løsepenger på 300 millioner naira. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
